sermon.title: Four Heavyweights
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: In “Four Heavyweights,” Pastor David G. Kincer teaches from Matthew 23:23 that the weightier matters of the law that people omit are judgment, mercy, faith and love, and that the Bible is easier to understand when we look for them. He then explains three kinds of God’s law — spiritual, civil and shadow (ceremonial) laws — using Jonah and Nineveh, Solomon’s judgment and the bond woman of Leviticus 19, and walks through Romans 6 and 8 to show which law we are not under and what each law is still for.

Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added by hand, and obvious caption errors were corrected; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes on references: at about 3:15 the captions read “Matthew 25. 23:15”, which is Matthew 23:15; at about 4:10 “John 81” is John 8:1 (the story runs John 8:1-11, shown). At about 6:23 the captions have him saying Jesus, “moved with compassion,” “began to give them money so they could be richer”; Mark 6:34 says He began to teach them many things, and he says in the next sentence that Jesus “had compassion and taught them,” so this may be a caption error or an aside; the transcript is kept as captioned. At about 14:21 he gives “Romans 10:13” for “Love does no harm to his neighbor, therefore love fulfills the law”; those words are Romans 13:10, so that passage is shown. At about 25:33 he goes to “the next chapter, 26th verse” (Leviticus 20:26) and then “verse 20” about the bond woman, which is Leviticus 19:20-22; both are shown. At about 29:02 he says “Hebrews 2:8” for “For by grace are you saved through faith”; those words are Ephesians 2:8-9, which he names at about 32:13, so that passage is shown. In the Leviticus bond-woman passage the captions give the number of years as “s years”; this is marked [unclear]. The captions read “uniform” for what the context shows is “cuneiform” and this was corrected. He quotes Matthew 18:27, Luke 11:42, 1 Timothy 2:8, 2 Corinthians 11:2 and Matthew 5:16 without naming the reference, and the sermon’s claims about archaeology, history, politicians, other religions and churches are his own and have not been checked by this site. Where he reads Scripture aloud his wording often differs slightly from the NKJV text shown with each section.

faqs.question: What is “Four Heavyweights” about?
faqs.answer: He teaches from Matthew 23:23 that the weightier matters of the law are judgment, mercy, faith and love, and then explains the different kinds of God’s law and which law we are not under.

scriptures.text_nkjv: “Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you pay tithe of mint and anise and cummin, and have neglected the weightier matters of the law: justice and mercy and faith. These you ought to have done, without leaving the others undone.

faqs.question: Why does he say people find the Bible hard to understand?
faqs.answer: He says preachers and people, himself included, had made the Bible way too difficult, and that if you look for the weightier matters you will start understanding it.

faqs.question: What does he say judgment is?
faqs.answer: He defines it as the decision for or against anything, and says you can be for it or against it but you are making a judgment.

faqs.question: What did Jesus do with the woman caught in adultery?
faqs.answer: He says Jesus told them, “Any of you without sin, go ahead and cast the first stone,” and then made a judgment not to stone her, but told her to go and sin no more.

scriptures.text_nkjv: But Jesus went to the Mount of Olives. Now early in the morning He came again into the temple, and all the people came to Him; and He sat down and taught them. Then the scribes and Pharisees brought to Him a woman caught in adultery. And when they had set her in the midst, they said to Him, “Teacher, this woman was caught in adultery, in the very act. Now Moses, in the law, commanded us that such should be stoned. But what do You say?” This they said, testing Him, that they might have something of which to accuse Him. But Jesus stooped down and wrote on the ground with His finger, as though He did not hear. So when they continued asking Him, He raised Himself up and said to them, “He who is without sin among you, let him throw a stone at her first.” And again He stooped down and wrote on the ground. Then those who heard it, being convicted by their conscience, went out one by one, beginning with the oldest even to the last. And Jesus was left alone, and the woman standing in the midst. When Jesus had raised Himself up and saw no one but the woman, He said to her, “Woman, where are those accusers of yours? Has no one condemned you?” She said, “No one, Lord.” And Jesus said to her, “Neither do I condemn you; go and sin no more.”

faqs.question: What is mercy?
faqs.answer: He says mercy is a lot like love, an outward expression of compassion to a person afflicted.

scriptures.text_nkjv: And Jesus, when He came out, saw a great multitude and was moved with compassion for them, because they were like sheep not having a shepherd. So He began to teach them many things.

faqs.question: Does Jesus only forgive, or does He also set us free?
faqs.answer: He says Jesus wants to forgive you and also loose, free and liberate you, rather than leave you in your sin.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Then the master of that servant was moved with compassion, released him, and forgave him the debt.

faqs.question: How does he say we are to love our enemies?
faqs.answer: He says we love our enemies in a different way, such as helping with a donkey in a ditch or a broken-down car, without having to invite them into our home to influence our kids for evil.

faqs.question: What is the simplest summary of the law?
faqs.answer: He says the whole law can be understood by not doing anything that hurts others or yourself, because love does no harm to his neighbor.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Love does no harm to a neighbor; therefore love is the fulfillment of the law.

faqs.question: What does love not do, according to 1 Corinthians 13?
faqs.answer: He lists that love is not jealous, proud, rude, demanding of its own way, or easily angered, and keeps no record of wrongs.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Love suffers long and is kind; love does not envy; love does not parade itself, is not puffed up; does not behave rudely, does not seek its own, is not provoked, thinks no evil;

faqs.question: What does he say faith simply means?
faqs.answer: He says faith simply means persuasion: being persuaded and convinced of moral truths in the Bible.

scriptures.text_nkjv: and being fully convinced that what He had promised He was also able to perform.

faqs.question: What good is knowledge without application?
faqs.answer: He says knowledge, understanding and education do no good if there is no application, and that faith should stand in the power of God and not the wisdom of men.

scriptures.text_nkjv: that your faith should not be in the wisdom of men but in the power of God.

faqs.question: What are statutes, commandments and spiritual laws?
faqs.answer: He says statutes are usually connected with religious ceremonies and rituals, commandments are the civil laws including the Ten Commandments, and spiritual laws bring me into relationship and connection with God.

faqs.question: What did Nineveh do when Jonah preached?
faqs.answer: He says all 120,000 believed God, proclaimed a fast by the king’s decree, prayed to God Jehovah and turned from their evil ways and violence, and God did not destroy them.

scriptures.text_nkjv: And Jonah began to enter the city on the first day’s walk. Then he cried out and said, “Yet forty days, and Nineveh shall be overthrown!” So the people of Nineveh believed God, proclaimed a fast, and put on sackcloth, from the greatest to the least of them. Then word came to the king of Nineveh; and he arose from his throne and laid aside his robe, covered himself with sackcloth and sat in ashes. And he caused it to be proclaimed and published throughout Nineveh by the decree of the king and his nobles, saying, Let neither man nor beast, herd nor flock, taste anything; do not let them eat, or drink water. But let man and beast be covered with sackcloth, and cry mightily to God; yes, let every one turn from his evil way and from the violence that is in his hands. Who can tell if God will turn and relent, and turn away from His fierce anger, so that we may not perish? Then God saw their works, that they turned from their evil way; and God relented from the disaster that He had said He would bring upon them, and He did not do it.

faqs.question: Does being saved by grace mean sin has no control over me?
faqs.answer: He says when I am under grace’s control, grace is power and sin doesn’t have control over me, and Romans 6 says “God forbid” to sinning because of grace.

scriptures.text_nkjv: What then? Shall we sin because we are not under law but under grace? Certainly not!

faqs.question: Are we still under civil and spiritual laws?
faqs.answer: He says yes, we still have no right to break civil laws and we still pray, fast, go to church and worship, but those laws will not free us from sin.
